comments.author: @leeltd
comments.text: I'm not a F1 fan but I found your video very interesting.  However, F1 is not the pioneer of focusing on drivers and teams to garner interest.  You need to research the popularity explosion of MotoGP from early 2000's through the early 2010's in spite of the fact that half the seasons were dominated by one team.  The social networking wasn't probably as savvy as F1, but MotoGP did drive attention to the personalities and conflicts of their racers.  A lot of that had to do with the cult of personality of Valentino Rossi, but that started the drive by fans to know the other competitors which in turn brought in a lot more fans.  MotoGP did some actions to facilitate that but a lot more were done by the racing teams.  The support media outlets also did a lot to focus on the drivers personalities instead of the technical aspects of racing, especially some of the drama.  I don't know any F1 drivers (except Hamilton) but another big factor was that there were A LOT of interesting characters in the paddock.
